memo.summary: The model discriminates well on a held-out test sample, beats a logistic regression benchmark modestly, and is well calibrated with stable scores. The main concerns are fair-lending outcomes at the recommended cutoff, which fall below the four-fifths screen for age and marital status, and the lack of any out-of-time validation.

findings.title: Approval rates differ by age band and marital status at the recommended cutoff
findings.text: At the 13% cutoff the adverse-impact ratio is 0.786 for age band and 0.704 for marital status, both below the 0.80 four-fifths screen. Approval among non-defaulters is also lower for the 21-29 and 50+ bands and for the Other marital group, so the gap is not explained by default risk alone. Age and marital status are not model inputs, but proxies in the inputs could still drive this. Fair-lending review is needed before use, including a check of which inputs carry the difference.

findings.title: No out-of-time validation sample
findings.text: All accounts come from the same six-month window, April to September 2005, and the split into training, validation and test is random. Performance and stability therefore say nothing about how the model holds up across economic conditions or later periods. An out-of-time sample should be obtained before the model is relied on for the full portfolio.

findings.title: Discrimination is adequate and the gap to the benchmark is small
findings.text: Test AUC is 0.768 and the training-to-test gap is 0.019, within the usual range, so overfitting is not a concern. The model beats the logistic benchmark by 0.016 AUC, a modest but statistically separated margin. The three top inputs are standard payment-behaviour fields with documented meanings.

findings.title: Calibration, rank ordering and monotonicity are sound
findings.text: The mean predicted default rate matches the observed rate on the test sample, with a calibration slope near 1 and a maximum decile gap of 2.9 points. Default rates rise almost monotonically across deciles, and no input moved the score against its expected direction.
